value: S152-001: caller-supplied from is not answer authority; independently bind sender and reject forged holder identity before answered_at mutation, with native/shim normal/FYI adversarial controls.

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Security verdict: BLOCK

PR: #152
Head: 253374c27943f039df593a46919ff2ecb2fb1cb1
Scope: full PR-owned security review against main c3895da518aad2047749b87dc9c6663592e357e2. Source verified at the frozen head.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs | 850-858 | Forged sender identity marks another holder's request answered | 9/10 |

S152-001: reply-accounting authority comes from an unverified sender string.

The direct local /v1/send path authenticates the machine but accepts caller-supplied from values other than the reserved daemon actor (http/mod.rs:1797-1858). After successful FYI holding (:1883-1893) or normal admission (:1958-1969), the new side effect passes that string into answer accounting. delivery/role_send.rs:850-858 checks that the request was delivered and its stored holder equals from, without independently proving the caller is that holder.

A locally authenticated seat A can send a fresh FYI to itself, claim from=B, and correlate it with a delivered request assigned to B. The FYI is held for A, yet the request is durably stamped answered (store/role_requests.rs:579-600), suppressing its limit check-in and PA escalation (:381-420). A need not own B's process, pane or session.

Required repair: independently bind the reply actor to the caller, reject mismatched sender claims, and enforce the intended stored-holder authority before stamping answered_at. Add native/shim and normal/FYI negative controls with correct victim sender identifiers and inherited-parent claims; each must leave answered_at unchanged. Retain a legitimate holder positive control and idempotence with output --answers. The current directory_http.rs:4139-4174 case tests an honestly named non-holder, not a forged holder.

Other requested boundaries:
- Cross-seat steering management is explicitly permitted by http/steer.rs:3-7,121-177. That broad switch-management policy does not authorize answering another holder's requests.
- Normal sends retain cold/force admission before enqueueing (http/mod.rs:1930-1962). This finding uses FYI holding and does not demonstrate a cold-guard or steering bypass.
- The off switch intentionally restores the previous pij-owned-turn barrier, not a blanket prohibition on the first injection into a human-started turn.
- Separate correctness/performance blocks remain independently owned: fleet-after-limit starvation, role-reply accounting omission, accepted/unconsumed abort recovery, stale on-to-off claim waits, and observer/poll costs. They are not relabelled here as additional security vulnerabilities.

Evidence and limitations:
- Exact-head CI run 42368599513 and latest Delivers 42368921695 independently verified SUCCESS. Green cases do not prove sender ownership against a caller supplying the correct holder name.
- CI: https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42368599513
- Delivers: https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42368921695
- Canary evidence uses a local fixture model, not hosted-provider or after-deployment proof. No canary rerun or live cost claim is made.
- No local builds/tests, runtime exploit probes, credential-file reads or product edits. GitHub's mergeStateStatus was UNKNOWN at the publication check; exact head and successful CI were verified separately.
